decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 1.75% to 2%. The vote was 7-3. Dissenting: James Bullard, Esther L. George, Eric S. Rosengren.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been risi…”

changes.quote: Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports have weakened.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Although growth of household spending has picked up from earlier in the year, growth of business fixed investment has been soft.”

changes.quote: In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target ran…”

changes.quote: Voting against the action were James Bullard, who preferred at this meeting to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent; and Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred to maintain the target range at 2 percent to 2-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Committee will conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings in the System Open Market Account in August, two months earlier than previously indicated.

tone_quotes.quote: In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent.

As the Committee contemplates the future path of the target range for the federal funds rate, it will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook and will act as appropriate to sustain the expansion, with a strong labor market and inflation near its symmetric 2 percent objective.
Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.13% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.8% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.49% would fall by about $1.67 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 184k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (August 2019); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +5 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.03%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.01% on the day.
